intro: Pause for a moment at Sam'al, an ancient city in Gaziantep province, whose story runs from the 3rd millennium BC to the 7th century BC. This is Zincirli Höyük, capital of a Neo-Hittite kingdom, famed for the lions of its gateways.
history: The story of this mound reaches back to the Early Bronze Age. In the Neo-Hittite period it became the capital of the kingdom of Sam'al, and under Assyrian rule it flourished. Excavations here uncovered city walls, hilani palaces and celebrated inscriptions.
structure-1: You are now at the Hilani Palace. The hilani is a palace type of Neo-Hittite architecture, known for its pillared reception hall. Imagine visitors being received between those pillars.
structure-2: Now look at the Double Gate Reliefs, the carvings that adorned the paired gateway of Sam'al. Pause and picture the gateway they once framed.
structure-5: Here is the Royal Inscription, recording the deeds and glory of a king: a ruler's pride, carved in stone.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Gateway Lions, and take time to follow the line of the City Walls.
facts: Did you know? King Kilamuwa's inscription is one of the earliest Semitic-language texts found in Anatolia. The city's circular double walls make a plan with few parallels in the Near East. The inscriptions of kings Kilamuwa and Panamuwa are primary documents in the history of the Semitic languages, and here Phoenician, Aramaic and Luwian were all in use. And the famous gate lions? Today they are displayed in the museums of Berlin and Istanbul.
outro: This brings our tour of Sam'al to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have spoken for centuries; let them speak to those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
